subproblem.title: Boundaries of regions in class 𝒪: dimension, support and cycle condition (Simon 7.5.1)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, N, E ⊆ ℝ^P, ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P (n+1)) and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Assume U is open, InClassO n U N ξ_N (N an embedded C² (n+1)-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P, ξ_N a continuous unit orientation of its tangent spaces, (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ and N ∩ U ≠ ∅), E ⊆ N ∩ U, and T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(x)(dω(x)) dH^{n+1}(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N, H^{n+1} = μHE[n+1]). Then n + 1 ≤ P, spt T ⊆ U ∩ N, and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T; vacuous for n = 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U N E : Set (Euclid P)) (ξN : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → InClassO n U N ξN → E ⊆ N ∩ U → IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → n + 1 ≤ P ∧ T.support ⊆ U ∩ N ∧ BoundaryVanishes T
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 0 (C0) of the supplied proof of CodimensionOneRegularity: Simon 7.5.1 (T = ∂[[E]] in U, chapter-07.txt lines 746–756) together with Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301) and Ch. 2, §4 (embedded submanifolds). This is part A0 of the previously reviewed analytic core of this node, stated as its own theorem; minimality of T is not needed for it. No DAG declaration is used.

Notation.
- H^{n+1} := μHE[n+1]; for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), dω is its exterior derivative (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative), a smooth (n+1)-form with tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset).
- IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N means T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(x)(dω(x)) dH^{n+1}(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
- “T vanishes on W” means T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Z(T) is the union of all open W with closure W compact and contained in U on which T vanishes, and spt T := U ∖ Z(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.support).
- BoundaryVanishes T is True for n = 0; for n = j + 1 it says T.boundary = 0, where T.boundary(φ) = T(dφ) for φ ∈ 𝒟^j(U).

Proof. Fix P, n, U, N, E, ξ_N, T satisfying the hypotheses.
1. (n + 1 ≤ P.)
- InClassO gives N ∩ U ≠ ∅; pick y ∈ N ∩ U.
- IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) N, applied at y, gives an open V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}, an open W ∋ y and ψ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P with ψ(V) = W ∩ N and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V.
- V ≠ ∅, since y ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V). For any z ∈ V the linear map Dψ(z) : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P is injective, so n + 1 = dim ℝ^{n+1} ≤ dim ℝ^P = P.
2. (spt T ⊆ U ∩ N.) spt T ⊆ U by definition. Let x ∈ U ∖ N; we show x ∉ spt T.
- Since (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ and x ∈ U ∖ N, x ∉ closure N. As U is open and closure N is closed, there is r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ⊆ U ∖ closure N.
- W₀ := B_{r/2}(x) is open, and closure W₀ ⊆ closedBall(x, r/2) is compact and contained in U. Moreover W₀ ∩ N = ∅.
- Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W₀. Then tsupport dω ⊆ W₀. Every point of E lies in N (E ⊆ N ∩ U), hence outside W₀, so dω = 0 at every point of E and T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(dω) dH^{n+1} = 0.
- So T vanishes on W₀; hence x ∈ W₀ ⊆ Z(T), i.e. x ∉ spt T.
Thus spt T ⊆ U ∩ N.
3. (∂T = 0.) For n = 0, BoundaryVanishes T is True. For n = j + 1 and φ ∈ 𝒟^j(U):
- T.boundary(φ) = T(dφ) = ∫_E ξ_N(d(dφ)) dH^{n+1} = ∫_E ξ_N(0) dH^{n+1} = 0, since d∘d = 0 (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_sq) and ξ_N(x) is linear.
- Currents agreeing on all test forms are equal, so T.boundary = 0.
Steps 1–3 are the three conjuncts. ∎
proof_key_steps: A chart of N at a point of N ∩ U has injective derivative ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P, so n + 1 ≤ P.
A point of U ∖ N has a ball, compactly contained in U, missing closure N; test forms supported there have dω = 0 on E, so T vanishes there and spt T ⊆ U ∩ N.
T(dφ) = ∫_E ξ_N(d(dφ)) = 0 since d∘d = 0, so ∂T = 0 (vacuous for n = 0).

audit.reason: A nonempty embedded chart gives the dimension inequality. Relative closedness of N supplies vanishing neighbourhoods outside N, and d² = 0 proves the cycle condition, with degree zero handled explicitly. No extra measurability or minimality assumption is required.

subproblem.title: Mass of a current given locally by integration over an oriented weighted set (Simon 6.2.5, 6.3.2(3))
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U, V, M' ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k), θ' : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k). Assume: V is open and V ⊆ U; M' is a Borel set with M' ⊆ V; θ' is Borel measurable with θ'(x) ≥ 0 for every x; ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for H^k⌞M' (H^k = μHE[k]); for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M' there is a linear subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(x)) Q (ξ'(x)(α) = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_k) for an orthonormal basis τ of Q); and T(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)) dH^k(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V. Then for every open W ⊆ V, with I(W) := ∫⁻_{M'∩W} ofReal(θ') dH^k ∈ [0, ∞]: (i) M_W(T) ≤ I(W), and (ii) if I(W) < ∞ then M_W(T) = I(W). Here M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U V M' : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (θ' : Euclid P → ℝ) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), IsOpen V → V ⊆ U → MeasurableSet M' → M' ⊆ V → Measurable θ' → (∀ x, 0 ≤ θ' x) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ' (μHE[k].restrict M') → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[k].restrict M'), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ' x) Q) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ⊆ V → T ω = ∫ x in M', θ' x * ξ' x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μHE[k]) → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ V → T.massOn W ≤ ∫⁻ x in M' ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ' x) ∂μHE[k] ∧ (∫⁻ x in M' ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ' x) ∂μHE[k] ≠ ∞ → T.massOn W = ∫⁻ x in M' ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ' x) ∂μHE[k])
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 6, 2.5 (the mass M_W) and 3.2(3) (for an integer multiplicity current, M_W(T) = μ_T(W)); chapter-06.txt lines 224–240 and 755–770. This is the argument of the facts (G5c) and (G6) of the previously reviewed analytic core of this node, written once with a general weight θ' in place of a constant multiplicity, so that the three analytic children region_density_one, simons_regular_cone and low_density_regular can cite it instead of re-proving it. It is needed because those children cannot use the parent's sibling im_mass_measure, and because they apply it to local pieces c·[[M']] that are not given by a global integer multiplicity representation.

Sibling child used (an accepted declaration, reused with its identical frozen type):
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): for all P, k there is a continuous linear map L : Λ_k(ℝ^P) → Λ^k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) k) such that for every ξ that is a unit orientation of some subspace Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q): (a) |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for every k-covector α; (b) |L(ξ)| ≤ 1; (c) ξ(L(ξ)) = 1.

Notation.
- H^k := μHE[k]; Λ^k := Covector (Euclid P) k, a finite-dimensional real vector space; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, the Euclidean coefficient norm, which is a norm on Λ^k (it is the Euclidean norm of the coordinate vector (α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_k}))_{I strictly increasing}, and these coordinates determine α by multilinearity and alternation).
- For an open W ⊆ V put I(W) := ∫⁻_{M'∩W} ofReal(θ') dH^k ∈ [0, ∞]. Since θ' ≥ 0, ofReal(θ') = θ'.
- M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}; such ω are called admissible for M_W(T).

Proof. Fix the data and hypotheses of the statement and an open W ⊆ V.

1. (Pointwise facts.) Let L be the map of unit_orientation_dual for (P, k). Let G ⊆ M' be the set of x ∈ M' at which ξ'(x) is a unit orientation of some subspace. By hypothesis M' ∖ G is contained in a Borel set Z with H^k(Z ∩ M') = 0. For every x ∈ G:
 (1a) |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^k;
 (1b) |L(ξ'(x))| ≤ 1;
 (1c) ξ'(x)(L(ξ'(x))) = 1.

2. (Upper bound: M_W(T) ≤ I(W).) If I(W) = ∞ there is nothing to prove; assume I(W) < ∞. Let ω be admissible for M_W(T).
- tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ V, so the hypothesis gives T(ω) = ∫_{M'} g dH^k with g(x) := θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)).
- Let x ∈ G. If x ∉ W, then x ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and g(x) = 0. If x ∈ W, then |g(x)| ≤ θ'(x)|ω(x)| ≤ θ'(x) by (1a). Hence |g| ≤ θ'·1_W at H^k-a.e. point of M'.
- θ'·1_W is integrable on M' with integral I(W) < ∞ (θ' ≥ 0 is measurable and W is Borel). So g is integrable on M' and T(ω) = ∫_{M'} g dH^k ≤ ∫_{M'} θ'1_W dH^k = I(W).
- Hence ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ I(W), and taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M_W(T) ≤ I(W).
This proves the first conclusion.

3. (Lower bound when I(W) < ∞.) Assume I(W) < ∞ and fix ε > 0.
(3a) ν := θ'·H^k⌞(M' ∩ W), i.e. ν(A) = ∫⁻_{M'∩W∩A} θ' dH^k, is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(ℝ^P) = I(W). A finite Borel measure on the Polish space ℝ^P is inner regular with respect to compact sets. Moreover ν(Z) = 0, because ν ≪ H^k⌞M'.
(3b) (Lusin.) The map h := L∘ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ^k is ν-a.e. strongly measurable, since L is continuous, ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for H^k⌞M', and ν ≪ H^k⌞M'. By Lusin's theorem for the finite inner regular measure ν and the map h into the finite-dimensional space Λ^k, applied inside the Borel set (M' ∩ W) ∖ Z, there is a compact K ⊆ (M' ∩ W) ∖ Z ⊆ G ∩ W with ν((M' ∩ W) ∖ K) < ε such that h restricted to K is continuous.
(3c) (Extension.) Fix a basis of Λ^k and apply the Tietze extension theorem to each coordinate of h|_K. This gives a continuous α₀ : ℝ^P → Λ^k with α₀ = h on K. Put α₁(y) := α₀(y)/max{1, |α₀(y)|}. Then α₁ is continuous, |α₁| ≤ 1 everywhere, and α₁ = h on K, because |h| ≤ 1 on K ⊆ G by (1b).
(3d) (Smoothing.) Let ρ_j ≥ 0 be smooth with ∫ρ_j = 1 and support in B_{1/j}(0), and put α_j := α₁ * ρ_j (coordinatewise convolution). Each α_j is smooth; |α_j(y)| ≤ ∫|α₁(y − z)|ρ_j(z) dz ≤ 1 because |·| is a norm; and α_j(y) → α₁(y) for every y, by continuity of α₁.
(3e) (Cut-off.) K is a compact subset of the open set W. By the smooth Urysohn lemma choose φ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on K, and tsupport φ a compact subset of W. Put ω_j := φ·α_j. Then ω_j is a smooth k-form with compact tsupport ω_j ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ W ⊆ V ⊆ U, so ω_j ∈ 𝒟^k(U), and |ω_j| ≤ φ|α_j| ≤ 1. Thus ω_j is admissible for M_W(T), and ofReal(T(ω_j)) ≤ M_W(T) for every j.
(3f) (Passage to the limit.) By hypothesis T(ω_j) = ∫_{M'} θ'φ·ξ'(α_j) dH^k (the integrand evaluated at x is θ'(x)φ(x)ξ'(x)(α_j(x))). For x ∈ G the integrand is bounded by θ'(x)1_W(x), by (1a), |α_j| ≤ 1 and φ = 0 off W; this dominant is integrable on M' with integral I(W) < ∞. The integrand converges pointwise to θ'φ·ξ'(α₁), since each ξ'(x) is continuous. By dominated convergence, T(ω_j) → J := ∫_{M'} θ'φ·ξ'(α₁) dH^k.
(3g) (Estimate of J.) Off W the integrand of J vanishes because φ = 0 there. On K we have φ = 1 and α₁ = L(ξ'), so the integrand equals θ' by (1c). At H^k-a.e. point of (M' ∩ W) ∖ K the integrand is ≥ −θ', by (1a), |α₁| ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1. Hence
 J ≥ ν(K) − ν((M' ∩ W) ∖ K) ≥ (I(W) − ε) − ε = I(W) − 2ε.
(3h) ofReal is continuous, so ofReal(J) = lim ofReal(T(ω_j)) ≤ M_W(T). Hence M_W(T) ≥ ofReal(I(W) − 2ε) for every ε > 0, and M_W(T) ≥ I(W).
Together with step 2, M_W(T) = I(W) whenever I(W) < ∞. This proves the second conclusion. ∎

subproblem.title: Zero-scale limits of blow-ups of codimension-one boundaries with moving centres are boundaries of regions in offset planes (Simon 7.5.3–7.5.5)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, U, N, E ⊆ ℝ^P, ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P), T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ U, points x_i → x of ℝ^P, scales λ_i > 0 with λ_i → 0, and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume U is open, InClassO n U N ξ_N, E is measurable with E ⊆ N ∩ U, T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(y)(dω(y)) dH^{n+1}(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N), and (a) there are C ∈ ℝ and r₀ > 0 with M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Cρ^n) (T.massOn (ball y ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C·ρ^n)) for all y ∈ B_{r₀}(x) and 0 < ρ < r₀; (b) the blow-ups η_{x_i,λ_i#}T (blowUp T x_i λ_i, η_{y,λ}(w) = λ^{−1}(w − y)) converge weakly to S in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); (c) spt S ≠ ∅. Then there are a linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P with dim Q = n + 1, a ∈ ℝ^P, a Borel set F ⊆ ℝ^P and ξ_A ∈ Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) such that, with A := {y : y + a ∈ Q} = Q − a: InClassO n ℝ^P A (y ↦ ξ_A) (A is an affine (n+1)-plane in class 𝒪 of ℝ^P, oriented by the constant ξ_A); F ⊆ A; and S = ∂[[F]] in ℝ^P, i.e. S(ω) = ∫_F ξ_A(dω(y)) dH^{n+1}(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) (IsBoundaryOfRegion S F (y ↦ ξ_A)).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 3 (C2(ii)) of the supplied proof of CodimensionOneRegularity, departure [D4]: zero-scale limits of blow-ups with moving centres are boundaries of regions in offset tangent planes. This is the codimension-one compactness argument of Simon 7.5.3–7.5.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 790–901), using the BV compactness theorem Ch. 2, 2.6 (chapter-02.txt lines 598–625) and lower semicontinuity of the variation (Ch. 2, §2; SimonGMT Chapter02.bvVariationOn_le_liminf_of_locallyL1). It is part A2 of the previously reviewed analytic core of this node, with these changes: the hypotheses on T are only those used (no minimality of T, and no hypothesis on S other than nonempty support); the conclusion stops at S = ∂[[F]] in the offset plane A = Q − a, which lies in class 𝒪 of ℝ^P. The parent then applies the sibling children region_support_cycle and region_density_one to S (U := ℝ^P, N := A, E := F) to get spt S ⊆ A and dense density-one points, exactly as the supplied step 3 ends with “as in step 1 with N replaced by A”. The linear inclusion of parent step 4 (0 ∈ spt S forces a ∈ Q) is also left to the parent.
Departure from parent step 3(α): the uniform local mass bound (a) is a hypothesis, replacing the monotonicity constant “Λ for K := closedBall x (2δ₀)”; the parent supplies (a) from the sibling monotonicity (i).

Sibling children used (accepted declarations, reused with their identical frozen types).
- hausdorff_dilation (Submission.dtc_hausdorff_dilation): for x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and d ∈ ℕ, Measure.map (dilation x λ) μHE[d] = ofReal(λ^d)·μHE[d] (part (ii)).
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): a continuous linear L : Λ_k → Λ^k with |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|, |L(ξ)| ≤ 1 and ξ(L(ξ)) = 1 for every unit orientation ξ of a subspace.
- orientation_sign (Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg): two unit orientations of the same subspace satisfy w = v or w = −v.

Notation.
- H^d := μHE[d]; on a d-dimensional affine plane it is d-dimensional Lebesgue measure. ω_d := unitBallVolume d. B_ρ(y) := ball y ρ. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector; M_W(T) := T.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ 1 pointwise (admissible ω).
- “T vanishes on W” means T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W; spt T := U ∖ Z(T), Z(T) the union of the open W with compact closure in U on which T vanishes.
- η_{y,λ}(w) := λ^{−1}(w − y) (dilation y λ). blowUp T y λ = η_{y,λ#}T ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{y,λ}(U)) acts by η_{y,λ#}T(ω) = T(η_{y,λ}^#ω).
- S_i ⇀ S (ConvergesWeakly) means currentEval(S_i)(ω) → S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), where currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(ω) if tsupport ω lies in the domain of S_i, and 0 otherwise.

Lemma (A-plane: affine planes with a constant unit orientation lie in class 𝒪 of ℝ^P). Let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace and ξ ∈ Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, let a ∈ ℝ^P, and put A := {y : y + a ∈ Q}. Then InClassO n ℝ^P A (y ↦ ξ).
1. Choose τ : Fin(n+1) → ℝ^P orthonormal with span τ = Q. Put ι(v) := Σ_i v_iτ_i and ψ(v) := ι(v) − a for v ∈ ℝ^{n+1}. |ι(v)|² = Σ_i v_i², so ι is an injective linear isometry with range Q (and dim Q = n + 1); ψ(ℝ^{n+1}) = A.
2. Embedded chart. For y ∈ A take V := ℝ^{n+1}, W := ℝ^P and the chart ψ: ψ is affine, hence C^∞; it is injective with ψ(V) = W ∩ A; Dψ = ι is injective; for compact K, ψ^{−1}(K) is closed and bounded (|v| = |ψ(v) + a| ≤ max_K|·| + |a|), hence compact. So IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) A.
3. A is the preimage of the closed subspace Q under y ↦ y + a, so closure A = A and (closure A ∖ A) ∩ ℝ^P = ∅. Also −a ∈ A, so A ∩ ℝ^P ≠ ∅.
4. tangentSpace(A, y) = Q for y ∈ A: if γ is C¹ with values in A and γ(0) = y, then t^{−1}(γ(t) − γ(0)) ∈ Q and Q is closed, so γ'(0) ∈ Q; conversely for v ∈ Q the curve γ(t) := y + tv lies in A with γ'(0) = v.
5. The constant map y ↦ ξ is continuous and is a unit orientation of Q = tangentSpace(A, y) at every y ∈ A; so IsOrientation (n+1) A (y ↦ ξ).
Steps 2–5 are the four conjuncts of InClassO n ℝ^P A (y ↦ ξ).

Proof. Fix the data and hypotheses of the statement; write (a) for the mass bound with constants C, r₀, (b) for S_i ⇀ S, and (d) for spt S ≠ ∅.
Set-up. Put η_i := η_{x_i,λ_i}, S_i := η_{i#}T and c_* := max{C, 0}. Passing to a subsequence is harmless throughout: S is the weak limit of every subsequence, and x_i → x, λ_i → 0 persist. Fix δ₀ > 0 with closedBall(x, 2δ₀) ⊆ U. For i large (|x_i − x| < δ₀), B_{δ₀}(x_i) ⊆ U, hence η_i(U) ⊇ B_{δ₀/λ_i}(0).
1. (Representation of S_i.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ η_i(U).
- S_i(ω) = T(η_i^#ω), where η_i^#ω is the affine pull-back (SimonGMT affinePullbackForm with linear part λ_i^{−1}I and translation −λ_i^{−1}x_i), because blowUp is the affinePushforward of T restricted to η_i^{−1}(η_i(U)) = U. Its tsupport is η_i^{−1}(tsupport ω) ⊆ U. By multilinearity, (η_i^#β)(y) = λ_i^{−j}β(η_i(y)) for every j-form β.
- d commutes with affine pull-back (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm), so d(η_i^#ω) = η_i^#(dω) = λ_i^{−(n+1)}(dω)∘η_i, and S_i(ω) = ∫_E λ_i^{−(n+1)} ξ_N(y)(dω(η_i(y))) dH^{n+1}(y).
- Change of variables. η_i is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse w ↦ x_i + λ_iw, and by hausdorff_dilation (ii) in dimension n + 1, η_{i#}H^{n+1} = λ_i^{n+1}H^{n+1}. Hence ∫ f(η_i(y)) dH^{n+1}(y) = λ_i^{n+1}∫ f dH^{n+1} for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ; this identity of Bochner integrals needs no integrability assumption (integration along the measurable equivalence η_i, Mathlib integral_map_equiv, then integral_smul_measure).
- Apply it to f(w) := 1_{E_i}(w)·λ_i^{−(n+1)}ξ_N(x_i + λ_iw)(dω(w)), E_i := η_i(E): since y ∈ E ⟺ η_i(y) ∈ E_i and x_i + λ_iη_i(y) = y, with ξ_i(w) := ξ_N(x_i + λ_iw) we get
 S_i(ω) = ∫_{E_i} ξ_i(w)(dω(w)) dH^{n+1}(w).
- Put N_i := η_i(N). If ω vanishes on an open set O' containing E_i ∩ tsupport ω (in particular if tsupport ω ∩ N_i = ∅), then S_i(ω) = 0, since dω = 0 on O' and off tsupport ω.
2. (Uniform mass bounds from (a).)
(2a) Let W be open with η_i^{−1}(W) ⊆ U and ω admissible for M_W(S_i). Then (η_i^#ω)(y) = λ_i^{−n}ω(η_i(y)), so λ_i^nη_i^#ω is admissible for M_{η_i^{−1}(W)}(T) (pointwise norm ≤ 1, tsupport a compact subset of η_i^{−1}(W) ⊆ U). Hence S_i(ω) = λ_i^{−n}T(λ_i^nη_i^#ω) ≤ λ_i^{−n}M_{η_i^{−1}(W)}(T), i.e. M_W(S_i) ≤ λ_i^{−n}M_{η_i^{−1}(W)}(T).
(2b) For W := B_ρ(0), η_i^{−1}(W) = B_{λ_iρ}(x_i). If x_i ∈ B_{r₀}(x), λ_iρ < r₀ and B_{λ_iρ}(x_i) ⊆ U, then (a) gives M_{B_ρ(0)}(S_i) ≤ λ_i^{−n}·c_*(λ_iρ)^n = c_*ρ^n.
3. (dist(x_i, N) = O(λ_i), and x ∈ N.) N ≠ ∅ since N ∩ U ≠ ∅. Suppose dist(x_i, N)/λ_i were unbounded; pass to a subsequence with dist(x_i, N)/λ_i → ∞, so dist(0, N_i) = dist(x_i, N)/λ_i → ∞. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0). For large i, tsupport ω ⊆ η_i(U), so currentEval(S_i)(ω) = S_i(ω), and B_R(0) ∩ N_i = ∅, so S_i(ω) = 0 by step 1. Hence S(ω) = 0 for every ω, S vanishes on every ball, and spt S = ∅, contradicting (d). So there is C₀ ≥ 1 with dist(x_i, N) ≤ C₀λ_i for all i. Letting i → ∞, dist(x, N) = 0, so x ∈ closure(N) ∩ U ⊆ N because (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅.
4. (Graph chart of N at x; parent 3(β).)
(4a) Tangent plane. IsOrientation (n+1) N ξ_N at x gives a subspace Π₀ with Π₀ = tangentSpace(N, x) and IsUnitOrientationOf(ξ_N(x), Π₀); dim Π₀ = n + 1. Put ξ_A := ξ_N(x), p := orthogonal projection onto Π₀, p^⊥ := I − p.
(4b) Take a chart (V, W, ψ) of N at x (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) N) and z₀ ∈ V with ψ(z₀) = x. ψ : V → W ∩ N is a continuous bijection with V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W; such a map is closed into the locally compact Hausdorff space W, so W ∩ N = ψ(V) is closed in W and ψ is a homeomorphism of V onto W ∩ N. For v ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and small ε > 0, t ↦ ψ(z₀ + εtv) is a C¹ curve in N through x with velocity εDψ(z₀)v, so range Dψ(z₀) ⊆ Π₀; Dψ(z₀) is injective and dim Π₀ = n + 1, so range Dψ(z₀) = Π₀.
(4c) By the inverse function theorem p∘(ψ − x) is a C² diffeomorphism of an open V₀ ∋ z₀ onto an open neighbourhood O of 0 in Π₀; ψ(V₀) ⊇ N ∩ B_s(x) for some s > 0 (ψ(V₀) is relatively open in W ∩ N). Put u := p^⊥∘(ψ − x)∘(p∘(ψ − x)|_{V₀})^{−1} : O → Π₀^⊥, a C² map with u(0) = 0 and Du(0) = 0. Choose r₁ > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r₁) ⊆ U ∩ W ∩ B_s(x), δ₂ := r₁, and δ₁ ∈ (0, r₁) with D := Π₀ ∩ B_{δ₁}(0) ⊆ O, |Du| ≤ 1 on D and |u| < δ₂/2 on D. The open cylinder Z := {x + v + h : v ∈ Π₀, |v| < δ₁, h ∈ Π₀^⊥, |h| < δ₂} has compact closure inside U ∩ W ∩ B_s(x).
(4d) Put Γ(v) := x + v + u(v) for v ∈ D. Then N ∩ Z = Γ(D) (a point q ∈ N ∩ Z lies in ψ(V₀), so v := p(q − x) ∈ D and q = Γ(v); conversely Γ(D) ⊆ N ∩ Z). Γ is an injective C² map with DΓ(v) = I + Du(v) on Π₀, and tangentSpace(N, Γ(v)) = DΓ(v)Π₀ (curves t ↦ Γ(v + εtw), and every C¹ curve γ in N through Γ(v) equals Γ∘(p∘(γ − x)) near t = 0).
(4e) Orientation formula. For v ∈ D let J(v) := det(DΓ(v)τ_i·DΓ(v)τ_j)^{1/2} > 0 for an orthonormal basis τ of Π₀ with ξ_A(β) = ±β(τ), and η(v)(α) := ξ_A(α(DΓ(v)·, …, DΓ(v)·))/J(v). Gram–Schmidt (DΓ(v)τ = σU, σ orthonormal, U upper triangular with positive diagonal, det U = J(v)) shows that η(v) is a unit orientation of DΓ(v)Π₀ = tangentSpace(N, Γ(v)). So is ξ_N(Γ(v)) (IsOrientation); by orientation_sign, ξ_N(Γ(v)) = s(v)η(v) with s(v) ∈ {±1}. With L from unit_orientation_dual, s(v) = ξ_N(Γ(v))(L(η(v))) is continuous on the connected set D (ξ_N continuous on N; Γ, DΓ, J continuous; L continuous), and s(0) = 1 because η(0) = ξ_A = ξ_N(x). Hence
 ξ_N(x + v + u(v)) = η(v) = Λ_{n+1}(I + Du(v))ξ_A/J(v) for all v ∈ D.
(4f) Rescaled graphs. Write x_i − x = s_i + t_i with s_i ∈ Π₀ and t_i ∈ Π₀^⊥; then s_i, t_i → 0. Put dom G_i := {w ∈ Π₀ : |s_i + λ_iw| < δ₁}, g_i(w) := λ_i^{−1}(u(s_i + λ_iw) − t_i) ∈ Π₀^⊥ and G_i(w) := w + g_i(w). Then:
- η_i(x + v + u(v)) = G_i(λ_i^{−1}(v − s_i)), so η_i(N ∩ Z) = G_i(dom G_i);
- p∘G_i = id and p^⊥∘G_i = g_i; G_i is injective;
- DG_i(w) = I + Du(s_i + λ_iw) on Π₀, so Dg_i(w) = Du(s_i + λ_iw) and |Dg_i| ≤ 1;
- x_i + λ_iG_i(w) = Γ(s_i + λ_iw), so by (4e) ξ_i(G_i(w)) = Λ_{n+1}DG_i(w)ξ_A/J_i(w), where J_i(w) := J(s_i + λ_iw) is the Jacobian of G_i.
5. (Offset; parent 3(γ).)
- Choose p_i ∈ N with |p_i − x_i| ≤ 2C₀λ_i. Then p_i → x, so for large i, p_i ∈ Z and p_i = x + v_i + u(v_i) with v_i ∈ D.
- w_i := λ_i^{−1}(v_i − s_i) ∈ dom G_i satisfies G_i(w_i) = η_i(p_i), and |η_i(p_i)| = |p_i − x_i|/λ_i ≤ 2C₀. Hence |w_i| = |p(G_i(w_i))| ≤ 2C₀ and |g_i(w_i)| ≤ 2C₀.
- For large i, dom G_i is convex and contains 0 and w_i, and |Dg_i| ≤ 1, so |g_i(0)| ≤ |g_i(w_i)| + |w_i| ≤ 4C₀.
- Pass to a subsequence with g_i(0) → −a, where a ∈ Π₀^⊥.
- Dg_i(w) = Du(s_i + λ_iw) → Du(0) = 0 uniformly for w in bounded sets. So g_i → −a and G_i → G, G(w) := w − a, in C¹ on Π₀ ∩ closedBall(0, R') for every R'.

6. (Local geometry; parent 3(δ).) Fix R ≥ 1, R₁ := R + |a| + 2 and C_R := {y : |p(y)| < R, |p^⊥(y)| < |a| + 1} ⊆ B_{R₁}(0). For all large i:

subproblem.title: Low-density points of minimizing currents are regular: Allard's theorem at the point (Simon 7.4.2–7.4.4 with Ch. 5, 5.2)
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ (d : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), n ≤ d → d ≤ P → IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N) → T.support ⊆ U ∩ N → BoundaryVanishes T → ∀ x ∈ T.support, ∀ θ : ℝ, HasMassDensity T x θ → θ < 1 + δ → x ∈ regularSet T)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This child supplies the one conclusion for which the supplied proof of CodimensionOneRegularity cites root theorems that the selected node cannot use: “x ∈ spt T and Θ^n(μ_T, x) < 1 + δ ⇒ x ∈ reg T”.
- In the supplied proof it is used in step 2 (⇐) for T itself, with d = n + 1, and in step 5(α) for the cone factor S₀, with U = N = ℝ^P and d = P.
- There it is derived from DensityAndTangentCones (2), the sibling density_gap and DensityOneImpliesRegular, which are not among this node's resolved dependencies.
Here it is proved by Simon's printed route instead: Allard's theorem 5.2 of Ch. 5 applied at the point itself, as in 7.4.2, 7.4.3 with T_j ≡ T and y_j ≡ y, and 7.4.4 (8) (“by Allard's 5.2 of Ch. 5 there is δ > 0 such that sing S = {Θ ≥ 1 + δ}”), with Lemma 7.1.2 justifying its use. The statement and the proof C0–C8 are those of the previously reviewed child low_density_regular of this node; only the citations of general facts changed.
Explicit departures from the parent text:
(i) No tangent cone, density gap or sequence version is needed. δ is Allard's constant for (n, P − n).
(ii) Stationarity along N and the bound on the generalized mean curvature are derived from minimality, by the printed proof of 7.1.2 together with Ch. 2, 5.6–5.10, instead of citing MinimizingImpliesStationary.
(iii) The mass–weight identity (C1b) is cited from the sibling child oriented_piece_mass instead of im_mass_measure.
No DAG declaration other than the four sibling children below is used.

Sibling children used.
- vanish_off_support (Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support): S(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt S = ∅.
- oriented_piece_mass (Submission.codim1_massOn_eq_lintegral_of_oriented_rep): if V ⊆ U is open, M' ⊆ V Borel, θ' ≥ 0 measurable, ξ' a.e. strongly measurable on M' and H^k-a.e. on M' a unit orientation of some subspace, and T(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ'·ξ'(ω) dH^k whenever tsupport ω ⊆ V, then for every open W ⊆ V: M_W(T) ≤ ∫_{M'∩W} θ' dH^k (first conclusion), with equality when the right side is finite (second conclusion).
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): a continuous linear L : Λ_k → Λ^k such that every unit orientation ξ of a subspace satisfies (a) |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for every k-covector α, (b) |L(ξ)| ≤ 1, (c) ξ(L(ξ)) = 1.
- orientation_sign (Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg): two unit orientations of the same subspace satisfy w = v or w = −v.

Notation.
- H^d := μHE[d]. On a d-dimensional affine plane it is d-dimensional Lebesgue measure, since Hausdorff measure is isometry invariant and μHE[d] = volume on ℝ^d. ω_d := unitBallVolume d is H^d of a unit d-disc.
- B_ρ(y) := ball y ρ.
- For a k-covector α, |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm).
- For T ∈ 𝒟_k(U), M_W(T) := T.massOn W = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 pointwise}.
- “T vanishes on W” means T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Z(T) is the union of the open W with compact closure in U on which T vanishes, and spt T := U ∖ Z(T).
- “Θ^k(μ_T, y) = θ” means HasMassDensity T y θ: θ ≥ 0 and M_{B_ρ(y)}(T)/(ω_kρ^k) → θ as ρ ↓ 0.

General facts. Let U be open, k ∈ ℕ and T ∈ 𝒟_k(U).
(G2) Positive density forces support.
- If T vanishes on an open W, then M_{W'}(T) = 0 for every W' ⊆ W, since every admissible form gives the value 0.
- Let y ∈ U with Θ^k(μ_T, y) = θ > 0, and suppose y ∉ spt T. Then y lies in an open W on which T vanishes, so M_{B_t(y)}(T) = 0 for small t and the density is 0 ≠ θ. Hence y ∈ spt T.
(O1) Orientations of planes. Let f_1, …, f_k ∈ ℝ^P be linearly independent with span Π. Then ξ(α) := α(f_1, …, f_k)/det(f_i·f_j)^{1/2} defines a unit orientation of Π (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Π).
- Gram–Schmidt writes f = σU, with σ an orthonormal basis of Π and U upper triangular with positive diagonal.
- By multilinearity and alternation, α(f) = det(U)·α(σ). Also det(f_i·f_j)^{1/2} = det(UᵀU)^{1/2} = det U.
- So ξ(α) = α(σ).

Proof (steps C0–C8). Printed sources:
- Simon 7.4.2 (“an immediate consequence of The Allard Theorem 5.2 of Ch. 5 and Lemma 1.2”), chapter-07-source.txt lines 605–615;
- 7.4.3 with T_j ≡ T and y_j ≡ y (lines 617–632);
- 7.4.4 (8), “by Allard's 5.2 of Ch. 5 there is δ > 0 such that sing S = {Θ ≥ 1 + δ}” (lines 673–675);
- Lemma 7.1.2 and its printed proof (lines 29–68);
- Ch. 2, 5.6–5.10 (chapter-02-source.txt lines 1290–1360) and Ch. 4, 2.5–2.7, 3.14 (chapter-04-source.txt lines 160–212, 370–380): stationarity in N and the mean curvature H_N;
- Ch. 5, 5.1–5.2 (Allard; chapter-05-source.txt lines 1008–1031) and 7.1 (lines 1312–1366);
- Ch. 6, 2.34 (constancy; chapter-06-source.txt lines 569–604).
The general facts (G2) and (O1) above are used with k := n.

C0. (Choice of δ.) Fix P and n ≥ 1. If n > P there is no d with n ≤ d ≤ P, so the statement holds vacuously; assume n ≤ P and put ℓ := P − n and p := 2n > n.
- If ℓ = 0, put δ := 1.
- If ℓ ≥ 1, let δ₀, γ ∈ (0, 1) and C_A ≥ 1 be the constants δ₀(n, ℓ, p), γ(n, ℓ, p) and C(n, ℓ, p) of the Allard Regularity Theorem (Simon Ch. 5, 5.2). Put δ := min{δ₀, (2C_A)^{−(2n+2)}} > 0.
- Since δ ≤ δ₀, hypotheses 5.1 with constant δ imply the conclusion of 5.2, and its estimate then gives sup|Du| ≤ C_Aδ^{1/(2n+2)} ≤ 1/2.
δ depends only on P and n.
Now fix d, U, N, T as in the statement, x ∈ spt T and θ with Θ^n(μ_T, x) = θ < 1 + δ.
- T is integer multiplicity (first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn). Fix an IMRep R = (M_R, θ_R, ξ_R) of T, and let μ := μ_R be its weight, μ(A) = ∫_{M_R∩A} θ_R dH^n.
- V := v(M_R, θ_R) is the associated varifold, so μ_V = μ.

C1. (Mass and weight.)
(C1a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult).
(C1b) For every open W ⊆ U, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W), and M_W(T) = μ(W) if μ(W) < ∞. This is oriented_piece_mass (first and second conclusions) applied with V := U, M' := M_R, θ' := θ_R and ξ' := ξ_R: its hypotheses are IMRep.measurableSet_carrier, IMRep.carrier_subset, IMRep.measurable_mult (θ_R ≥ 0), IMRep.aestronglyMeasurable_orient, IMRep.orients (ξ_R(x) is a unit orientation of the approximate tangent plane for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M_R) and R.Represents T; and ∫_{M_R∩W} θ_R dH^n = μ(W).
(C1c) spt T = U ∩ spt μ, and μ(U ∖ spt T) = 0. Let y ∈ U and let r > 0 with closedBall(y, r) ⊆ U.
- If y ∉ spt T, then T vanishes on an open W ∋ y. For ε ≤ r with B_ε(y) ⊆ W, (C1b) and (G2) give μ(B_ε(y)) = M_{B_ε(y)}(T) = 0.
- If μ(B_ε(y)) = 0 for some ε ≤ r, then M_{B_ε(y)}(T) = 0 by (C1b), so T vanishes on B_ε(y): any ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ε(y) and T(ω) ≠ 0 would make ±ω/max|ω| admissible with positive value. Hence y ∉ spt T.
- U ∖ spt T is open and is covered by countably many such balls of μ-measure 0 (second countability). So μ(U ∖ spt T) = 0.
(C1d) For 0 < r with closedBall(x, r) ⊆ U, μ(B_r(x)) = M_{B_r(x)}(T), by (C1a) and (C1b).
(C1e) Tangent planes lie in T_yN.
- By (C1c), μ-a.e. y ∈ M_R lies in spt T ⊆ N. Since θ_R ≥ 1 on M_R, H^n(M_R ∖ N) = 0.
- At μ-a.e. y ∈ M_R ∩ N the approximate tangent space T_yM_R exists, and T_yM_R ⊆ T_yN. Indeed the blow-ups of H^n⌞M_R at y are carried by the blow-ups of N, up to the H^n-null set M_R ∖ N, and these converge to T_yN locally in Hausdorff distance.

C2. (First variation along N; Simon 7.1.2 and its printed proof.) Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^P) with X(y) ∈ T_yN for every y ∈ N ∩ U. Then ∫_{M_R} θ_R div_{M_R}X dH^n = 0.
(C2a) N ∩ U is relatively closed in U, because (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅. Hence N ∩ K is compact for every compact K ⊆ U.
(C2b) By Simon Ch. 2, the discussion preceding 5.8 (= Ch. 4, 2.5–2.6), there is a family φ_t, t ∈ (−1, 1), of diffeomorphisms of U such that:
- (t, y) ↦ φ_t(y) is C²;
- φ_t(U ∩ N) ⊆ U ∩ N and φ_0 = id;
- φ_t = id on U ∖ K for a compact K ⊆ U;
- the initial velocity Y := ∂_tφ_t|_{t=0} is a C¹ vector field with support in K and Y = X on N ∩ U. The book gives the initial velocity X at the points of N ∩ U.
Choose an open W ⊇ K with compact closure in U. Since φ_t is a bijection of U equal to the identity off K ⊆ W, φ_t(K) = K and φ_t(W) = W.
(C2c) The competitor. Put S_t(ω) := ∫_{M_R} θ_R ⟨ω(φ_t(y)), Λ_nDφ_t(y)ξ_R(y)⟩ dH^n(y) for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). This is φ_{t#}T (Simon Ch. 6, 3.3), i.e. T acting through its representation on the compactly supported C¹ form φ_t^#ω.
- S_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U). It is linear, and |S_t(ω)| ≤ c_n·sup|Dφ_t|^n·μ(K_ω ∪ K)·sup|ω| whenever tsupport ω ⊆ K_ω with K_ω compact (c_n a constant depending only on n and P), since φ_t^{−1}(K_ω) ⊆ K_ω ∪ K and |ξ_R(y)(α)| ≤ |α| for H^n-a.e. y ∈ M_R (IMRep.orients and unit_orientation_dual (a)). So it is continuous for test-form convergence.
- S_t is integer multiplicity. By the area formula on the countably n-rectifiable set M_R (Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9), S_t = τ(φ_t(M_R), θ_R∘φ_t^{−1}, ξ_t), where ξ_t(φ_t(y)) := Λ_nDφ_t(y)ξ_R(y)/|Λ_nDφ_t(y)ξ_R(y)|. Here φ_t(M_R) is Borel and countably n-rectifiable. Its approximate tangent space at φ_t(y) is Dφ_t(y)(T_yM_R) for H^n-a.e. y. The multiplicity is locally integrable because the Jacobians of φ_t and φ_t^{−1} are bounded on compact sets.
- ∂S_t = 0 = ∂T. Let ψ ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U).
  - φ_t^#ψ is a compactly supported C¹ form, and S_t(dψ) = T(φ_t^#dψ) = T(d(φ_t^#ψ)).
  - Mollifications η_j of φ_t^#ψ are test forms supported in a fixed compact subset of U, with dη_j → d(φ_t^#ψ) uniformly.
  - T(dη_j) = 0 because ∂T = 0. By dominated convergence in the representation, T(dη_j) → T(d(φ_t^#ψ)). So S_t(dψ) = 0.
- spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N.
  - If tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅, then S_t(ω) = T(ω): near every y ∈ M_R ∖ K the map φ_t is the identity, and ω vanishes at the points φ_t(y) ∈ K for y ∈ M_R ∩ K.
  - If tsupport ω ∩ N = ∅, then T(ω) = 0 by vanish_off_support, since spt T ⊆ N. Also S_t(ω) = 0: μ-a.e. y ∈ M_R lies in spt T ⊆ N by (C1c), so φ_t(y) ∈ N and ω(φ_t(y)) = 0.
  - U ∖ K and U ∖ N are open by (C2a). A smooth partition of unity subordinate to them splits any ω with tsupport ω ⊆ U ∖ (K ∩ N) into two such pieces. So S_t − T vanishes on U ∖ (K ∩ N).
  - Hence spt(S_t − T) is a relatively closed subset of U contained in the compact set K ∩ N ⊆ (U ∩ N) ∩ W, and so it is compact.
- Since T is minimizing in U ∩ N, M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S_t) for all t ∈ (−1, 1).
(C2d) Differentiation.
- By (C1b) for T, and by oriented_piece_mass (second conclusion) for S_t with its representation above (both weights of W are finite by (C1a) and the boundedness of the Jacobians), M_W(T) = μ(W).
- By the area formula, M_W(S_t) = ∫_{φ_t(M_R)∩W} θ_R∘φ_t^{−1} dH^n = ∫_{M_R∩W} θ_R J_t dH^n, where J_t(y) := |Λ_nDφ_t(y)τ(y)| for an orthonormal basis τ(y) of T_yM_R.
- So f(t) := ∫_{M_R∩W} θ_R J_t dH^n has a minimum at t = 0.
- J_t is C¹ in t, with J_0 = 1 and ∂_tJ_t|_{t=0} = div_{M_R}Y. Its t-derivative is bounded uniformly on K, J_t = 1 off K, and μ(W) < ∞. So f'(0) = ∫_{M_R} θ_R div_{M_R}Y dH^n (Simon Ch. 2, 5.1–5.3; Ch. 4, 2.2).
- div_{M_R}Y = div_{M_R}X μ-a.e. By (C1e), μ-a.e. y ∈ M_R lies in N with T_yM_R ⊆ T_yN. The C¹ field Y − X vanishes on the C¹ submanifold N, so its derivative at y vanishes along T_yN, hence along T_yM_R. So f'(0) = ∫_{M_R} θ_R div_{M_R}X dH^n.
- Since the minimum is interior, ∫_{M_R} θ_R div_{M_R}X dH^n = 0.

C3. (Bounded generalized mean curvature; Simon Ch. 2, 5.9–5.10; Ch. 4, 2.7, 3.14.)
(C3a) By (C1e), H^n(M_R ∖ N) = 0, and T_yM_R ⊆ T_yN at μ-a.e. y ∈ M_R.
(C3b) The mean curvature field. Let B^N be the second fundamental form of the C² submanifold N, with Simon's sign convention (Ch. 2, 4.24): B^N_y(τ, η) = −Σ_j (τ·D_ην^j)ν^j for a local orthonormal normal frame (ν^j). It is continuous on N. For y as in (C1e) put H(y) := Σ_{i=1}^n B^N_y(τ_i, τ_i), with τ an orthonormal basis of T_yM_R; put H := 0 elsewhere. H is μ-measurable.
(C3c) The first variation formula. Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^P).
- Cover the compact set N ∩ spt X by finitely many open cylinders O_k = {z₀ + v + h : v ∈ Π_k, |v| < r_k, h ∈ Π_k^⊥, |h| < r_k'} ⊆ U, with z₀ ∈ N and Π_k := T_{z₀}N. Choose them so that N ∩ O_k = {z₀ + v + w(v) : v ∈ Π_k, |v| < r_k} is the graph of a C² map w : Π_k ∩ B_{r_k}(0) → Π_k^⊥ with |w| < r_k'.
- Such cylinders exist. Take a chart (V, W, ψ) of N at z₀ (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N), so that Dψ(ψ^{−1}(z₀)) is injective with range Π_k (the curve argument shows range ⊆ T_{z₀}N, and the dimensions agree). By the inverse function theorem, p_k∘(ψ − z₀) is a C² diffeomorphism near ψ^{−1}(z₀), where p_k is the orthogonal projection onto Π_k. ψ is proper and injective, hence a homeomorphism onto W ∩ N, which is relatively closed in W. So for small r_k, r_k' with r_k' small relative to r_k, N ∩ O_k is exactly the graph of w := p_k^⊥∘(ψ − z₀)∘(p_k∘(ψ − z₀))^{−1}, and |w| < r_k'.
- Gram–Schmidt applied to the C¹ normal vectors of the graph gives a C¹ orthonormal frame (ν^j) of the normal spaces of N along N ∩ O_k. Extend it to O_k by ν^j(z₀ + v + h) := ν^j(z₀ + v + w(v)), which is C¹. Only derivatives along T_yN at points y ∈ N enter below, so the extension is immaterial.
- Take a C^∞ partition of unity subordinate to {O_k} ∪ {U ∖ N}, and write X = X₀ + Σ_k X_k, with X₀ vanishing on a neighbourhood of N and X_k ∈ C¹_c(O_k).
- div_{M_R}X₀ = 0 at every point of M_R ∩ N. Since H^n(M_R ∖ N) = 0, ∫ θ_R div_{M_R}X₀ dH^n = 0 = −∫ X₀·H dμ.
- For each k put X_k^T := X_k − Σ_j (X_k·ν^j)ν^j. It is C¹ with compact support in O_k and tangent to N on N ∩ O_k, so (C2) gives ∫ θ_R div_{M_R}X_k^T dH^n = 0.
- At μ-a.e. y ∈ M_R ∩ O_k, since ν^j(y) ⊥ T_yM_R, the computation of Simon Ch. 2, 5.9 gives div_{M_R}X_k = div_{M_R}X_k^T + Σ_j (X_k·ν^j)div_{M_R}ν^j = div_{M_R}X_k^T − X_k·H.
- Summing, ∫ θ_R div_{M_R}X dH^n = −∫ X·H dμ for every X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^P).
So V has generalized mean curvature H in U (Simon Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.14).
(C3d) Bound. For each compact K ⊆ U, |H| ≤ Λ_K := n·max_{N∩K}|B^N| < ∞ μ-a.e. on K. The maximum is finite because N ∩ K is compact (C2a).

C4. (Allard's hypotheses at x.) Assume ℓ ≥ 1. Choose ρ₀ > 0 with closedBall(x, ρ₀) ⊆ U, and put Λ := Λ_{closedBall(x, ρ₀)}.
- θ_R ≥ 1 on M_R, so the density of V is ≥ 1 μ_V-a.e.
- x ∈ spt μ by (C1c), i.e. x ∈ spt V.
- By (C1d), M_{B_r(x)}(T)/(ω_nr^n) = μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nr^n) for r ≤ ρ₀, and this tends to θ < 1 + δ. So there is ρ₁ ∈ (0, ρ₀) with (ω_nr^n)^{−1}μ(B_r(x)) ≤ 1 + δ for 0 < r < ρ₁.
- For such r, (r^{p−n}∫_{B_r(x)} |H|^p dμ)^{1/p} ≤ (r^{p−n}Λ^p(1 + δ)ω_nr^n)^{1/p} ≤ Λ(2ω_n)^{1/p}r.
- Fix ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁) with Λ(2ω_n)^{1/p}ρ ≤ δ. Then, after translating x to 0, the hypotheses 5.1 of Simon Ch. 5 hold for V with radius ρ and constant δ ≤ δ₀.

C5. (Allard's conclusion.)
- If ℓ ≥ 1, Theorem 5.2 of Ch. 5 gives a linear isometry q of ℝ^P = ℝ^n × ℝ^ℓ and u ∈ C^{1,1−n/p}(B^n_{γρ}(0); ℝ^ℓ) with spt μ ∩ B_{γρ}(x) = (x + q(graph u)) ∩ B_{γρ}(x) and sup|Du| ≤ 1/2 (C0).
  - Since x ∈ spt μ, x = x + q(v₀, u(v₀)) with |v₀| ≤ |q(v₀, u(v₀))| = 0. So u(0) = 0, and |u(v)| ≤ |v|/2.
  - By (C1c), spt T ∩ B_{γρ}(x) = (x + q(graph u)) ∩ B_{γρ}(x).
- If ℓ = 0, choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(x, ρ) ⊆ U and set γ := 1, q := id and u :≡ 0 ∈ ℝ^0 on B^n_ρ(0) = B^P_ρ(0). Then x + q(graph u) = B_ρ(x), so spt T ∩ B_{γρ}(x) ⊆ x + q(graph u) trivially; also u(0) = 0 and Du ≡ 0.
In both cases spt T ∩ B_{γρ}(x) ⊆ x + q(graph u), with u(0) = 0 and sup|Du| ≤ 1/2. Only this inclusion is used below.

C6. (The graph piece.) Put σ := γρ/2 and D := B^n_σ(0) ⊆ ℝ^n (identified with Euclid n). Define Γ(v) := x + q(v, u(v)) for v ∈ D, the affine map π(y) := (first n coordinates of q^{−1}(y − x)) from ℝ^P to ℝ^n, and M := Γ(D). Then π∘Γ = id_D and Dπ∘DΓ(v) = I.
(C6a) |v| ≤ |Γ(v) − x| ≤ (3/2)|v|, so M ⊆ B_{3σ/2}(x) ⊆ B_{γρ}(x). Moreover spt T ∩ B_σ(x) ⊆ M: a point y of the left side is Γ(v) with |v| ≤ |y − x| < σ.
(C6b) IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M, and x = Γ(0) ∈ M.
- Γ is C¹ on D and injective, since π∘Γ = id. DΓ(v)w = q(w, Du(v)w) is injective, since |DΓ(v)w| ≥ |w|.
- For every point of M use the chart (V, W, ψ) := (D, π^{−1}(D), Γ). W is open, and ψ(V) = M = W ∩ M.
- For compact K' ⊆ W, the set D ∩ Γ^{−1}(K') = {v ∈ π(K') : Γ(v) ∈ K'} is closed in the compact set π(K') ⊆ D, hence compact.
(C6c) tangentSpace(M, Γ(v)) = DΓ(v)(ℝ^n) for v ∈ D.
- (⊇) For w ∈ ℝ^n, let ε := (σ − |v|)/(1 + |w|) and h(t) := ε·tanh(t/ε). Then γ(t) := Γ(v + h(t)w) is a C¹ curve on (−1, 1) in M with γ(0) = Γ(v) and γ'(0) = DΓ(v)w.
- (⊆) If γ is a C¹ curve in M with γ(0) = Γ(v), then π∘γ is C¹ with values in D, and γ = Γ∘(π∘γ). So γ'(0) = DΓ(v)(π∘γ)'(0).
(C6d) IsOrientation n M ξ_M.
- For y ∈ M and v := π(y), put ξ_M(y)(α) := α(DΓ(v)e_1, …, DΓ(v)e_n)/J(v), with J(v) := det(DΓ(v)ᵀDΓ(v))^{1/2} > 0. Put ξ_M := 0 off M.
- Gram–Schmidt writes DΓ(v)e = σ'U with σ' an orthonormal basis of DΓ(v)ℝ^n and U upper triangular with positive diagonal, and det U = J(v). So ξ_M(y)(α) = α(σ'), and ξ_M(y) is a unit orientation of tangentSpace(M, y) by (O1).
- ξ_M is continuous on M, because DΓ, π and J are continuous and J > 0.
(C6e) H^n(M) = ∫_D J dL^n ≤ (5/4)^{n/2}ω_nσ^n < ∞, by the area formula and ‖DΓ‖² ≤ 1 + |Du|² ≤ 5/4. In particular H^n(M ∩ K'') < ∞ for every K''.

C7. (Constant integer multiplicity on M; constancy theorem.)
(C7a) μ(B_σ(x) ∖ M) = 0 by (C1c) and (C6a). Since θ_R ≥ 1 on M_R, H^n((M_R ∩ B_σ(x)) ∖ M) = 0.
(C7b) For H^n-a.e. y ∈ M_R ∩ M ∩ B_σ(x), the approximate tangent space of M_R at y is T_yM.
- At H^n-a.e. y ∈ M_R the upper density of H^n⌞(M ∖ M_R) is 0 (Simon Ch. 3, §1).
- Near y ∈ B_σ(x), H^n⌞M_R = H^n⌞M − H^n⌞(M ∖ M_R) by (C7a). So the blow-ups of H^n⌞M_R at such y have the limit H^n⌞T_yM.
- By IMRep.orients, ξ_R(y) is then a unit orientation of T_yM. Two unit orientations of one plane differ by a sign (orientation_sign), so ξ_R(y) = s(y)ξ_M(y) with s(y) ∈ {±1}.
(C7c) Put f := θ_R s on M_R ∩ M ∩ B_σ(x), and f := 0 on M ∖ (M_R ∩ B_σ(x)). f is H^n-measurable and integer valued, and ∫_M |f| dH^n ≤ μ(B_σ(x)) < ∞. By (C7a) and (C7b), every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_σ(x) satisfies T(ω) = ∫_{M_R} θ_R⟨ω, ξ_R⟩ dH^n = ∫_M f⟨ω, ξ_M⟩ dH^n.
(C7d) Constancy. Put D' := B^n_{σ/2}(0) and let β ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(D').
- Γ(spt β) ⊆ closedBall(x, 3σ/4) by (C6a).
- Choose χ ∈ C^∞_c(B_σ(x)) with χ = 1 on B_{7σ/8}(x), and put ω_β := χ·π^#β ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U).
- dω_β = χπ^#dβ + dχ∧π^#β. Let y ∈ M. If dχ(y) ≠ 0, then |y − x| ≥ 7σ/8, so π(y) ∉ spt β (otherwise y = Γ(π(y)) ∈ closedBall(x, 3σ/4)), and (π^#β)(y) = 0. Also χ(y) = 1 wherever (π^#dβ)(y) ≠ 0. Hence ⟨dω_β, ξ_M⟩ = ⟨π^#dβ, ξ_M⟩ on M.
- ∂T = 0 (n ≥ 1) and (C7c) give 0 = T(dω_β) = ∫_M f⟨π^#dβ, ξ_M⟩ dH^n.
- By the area formula for Γ, and because Dπ∘DΓ(v) = I gives ⟨(π^#dβ)(Γ(v)), ξ_M(Γ(v))⟩ = dβ(v)(e_1, …, e_n)/J(v), this integral equals ∫_D f(Γ(v))·dβ(v)(e_1, …, e_n) dv.
- Hence the n-current S'(α) := ∫_{D'} (f∘Γ)·α(e_1, …, e_n) dv on D' has ∂S' = 0. It is well defined: J ≥ 1 gives ∫_{D'}|f∘Γ| ≤ ∫_M |f| < ∞.
- By the constancy theorem (Simon Ch. 6, 2.34; D' is connected), S' = m[[D']] for a constant m, i.e. f∘Γ = m L^n-a.e. on D'. Since f is integer valued, m ∈ ℤ.
(C7e) Put ρ' := σ/2 and let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ'}(x).
- Every y ∈ M ∩ B_{ρ'}(x) has |π(y)| ≤ |y − x| < σ/2, i.e. y ∈ Γ(D').
- f = m H^n-a.e. on Γ(D'), by (C7d) and the area formula.
- So (C7c) gives T(ω) = m∫_{M∩B_{ρ'}(x)} ⟨ω, ξ_M⟩ dH^n = m∫_M ξ_M(y)(ω(y)) dH^n(y).
(C7f) m ≠ 0. Otherwise T vanishes on B_{ρ'}(x), whose closure is a compact subset of U, and x ∉ spt T.

C8. (Conclusion.) We have:
- x ∈ spt T;
- ρ' > 0 with B_{ρ'}(x) ⊆ U;
- m ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} and x ∈ M;
- IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M (C6b) and IsOrientation n M ξ_M (C6d);
- H^n(M ∩ K'') < ∞ for compact K'' ⊆ B_{ρ'}(x) (C6e);
- T(ω) = m∫_M ξ_M(ω) dH^n whenever tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ'}(x) (C7e).
This is x ∈ regularSet T. δ was chosen in C0 depending only on P and n. ∎
proof_key_steps: C0–C1: δ := 1 if P = n, else δ := min{δ₀, (2C_A)^{−(2n+2)}} from Allard's constants (p = 2n); mass equals weight on open sets of finite weight (oriented_piece_mass); spt T = U ∩ spt μ_T and μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0; tangent planes of the carrier lie in T_yN.

C2–C3: competitors φ_{t#}T for the book's families preserving N (Simon 7.1.2) give first variation zero along N; with Ch. 2, 5.9 the varifold has generalized mean curvature H = Σ B^N(τ_i, τ_i), bounded by n·max|B^N| on compact sets.
C4–C5: Θ(x) < 1 + δ and ρΛ small give Allard's hypotheses 5.1 at x; Theorem 5.2 puts spt T ∩ B_{γρ}(x) in the graph of a C¹ map u with u(0) = 0 and |Du| ≤ 1/2.

C6–C8: the graph piece M is an oriented embedded C¹ n-submanifold with finite area; T = ∫_M f⟨·, ξ_M⟩ with integer f (orientation_sign); testing ∂T = 0 on χπ^#β and the constancy theorem give f ≡ m ≠ 0 near x; hence x ∈ regularSet T.

subproblem.title: Boundaries of regions have density one on a dense subset of their support (Simon 7.5.2(‡))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, U, N, E ⊆ ℝ^P, ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Assume U is open, InClassO n U N ξ_N, E is measurable with E ⊆ N ∩ U, T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(x)(dω(x)) dH^{n+1}(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N), and T is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity T). Then for every x ∈ spt T and every ρ > 0 there is y ∈ spt T ∩ B_ρ(x) with Θ^n(μ_T, y) = 1 (HasMassDensity T y 1).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U N E : Set (Euclid P)) (ξN : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), 1 ≤ n → IsOpen U → InClassO n U N ξN → MeasurableSet E → E ⊆ N ∩ U → IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → ∀ x ∈ T.support, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ∃ y ∈ T.support ∩ ball x ρ, HasMassDensity T y 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 1 (C1) of the supplied proof of CodimensionOneRegularity: Simon 7.5.2 and its consequence (‡) “Θ^n(μ_T, x) = 1 for μ_T-a.e. x” (chapter-07.txt lines 757–770), which rests on Ch. 6, 2.35 (chapter-06.txt lines 606ff.) and De Giorgi's structure theorem, Ch. 3, 4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 588–606); densities of rectifiable sets are Ch. 3, 1.8(2)–1.9 (chapter-03.txt lines 298–323). This is part A1 of the previously reviewed analytic core of this node, stated as its own theorem. Departures from that text: the hypothesis is only that T is integer multiplicity (all that its proof used of minimality); the mass facts (G5c), (G6) are cited from the sibling child oriented_piece_mass; the Riesz map is replaced by the dual map of unit_orientation_dual. The conclusion is the form of 5.2(‡) used by the parent: density-one points are dense in spt T.

Sibling children used.
- region_support_cycle (Submission.codim1_region_support_cycle): under the hypotheses below, n + 1 ≤ P, spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0.
- oriented_piece_mass (Submission.codim1_massOn_eq_lintegral_of_oriented_rep): if V ⊆ U is open, M' ⊆ V Borel, θ' ≥ 0 measurable, ξ' a.e. strongly measurable on M' and H^k-a.e. on M' a unit orientation of some subspace, and T(ω) = ∫_{M'} θ'·ξ'(ω) dH^k whenever tsupport ω ⊆ V, then for every open W ⊆ V: M_W(T) ≤ ∫_{M'∩W} θ' dH^k, with equality when the right side is finite.
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): a continuous linear L : Λ_k → Λ^k with |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|, |L(ξ)| ≤ 1 and ξ(L(ξ)) = 1 for every unit orientation ξ of a subspace.
- orientation_sign (Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg): two unit orientations of the same subspace Q satisfy w = v or w = −v.

Notation.
- H^d := μHE[d]. On a d-dimensional affine plane it is d-dimensional Lebesgue measure (Hausdorff measure is isometry invariant and μHE[d] = volume on ℝ^d). ω_d := unitBallVolume d is H^d of a unit d-disc. B_ρ(y) := ball y ρ.
- For a k-covector α, |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm). M_W(T) := T.massOn W = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 pointwise}; such ω are admissible for M_W(T).
- “T vanishes on W” means T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Z(T) is the union of the open W with compact closure in U on which T vanishes, and spt T := U ∖ Z(T).
- “Θ^n(μ_T, y) = θ” means HasMassDensity T y θ: θ ≥ 0 and M_{B_ρ(y)}(T)/(ω_nρ^n) → θ as ρ ↓ 0.
- For an IMRep R = (M_R, θ_R, ξ_R) of T, μ_R(A) := ∫_{M_R∩A} θ_R dH^n; μ_R(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult).

General facts (T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open).
(G2) Positive density forces support. If T vanishes on an open W, then M_{W'}(T) = 0 for every W' ⊆ W, since every admissible form gives the value 0. Hence if y ∈ U has Θ^n(μ_T, y) = θ > 0 and y ∉ spt T, then y lies in an open W on which T vanishes, M_{B_t(y)}(T) = 0 for small t, and the density is 0 ≠ θ. So such y lies in spt T.
(G3) Mass near support points. Let x ∈ spt T and let W ∋ x be open with compact closure in U. Then T does not vanish on W (otherwise W ⊆ Z(T) ∋ x), so T(ω) ≠ 0 for some ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. With s := max|ω| > 0, one of ±ω/s is admissible for M_W(T) and has positive value; so M_W(T) > 0.
(G7) Density of rectifiable sets (Simon Ch. 3, 1.8(2), 1.9). If M' ⊆ ℝ^P is countably n-rectifiable and H^n-measurable with H^n(M') < ∞, then lim_{t↓0} H^n(M' ∩ B_t(w))/(ω_nt^n) = 1 for H^n-a.e. w ∈ M'.

Proof. Fix P, n ≥ 1, U, N, E, ξ_N, T satisfying the hypotheses, x ∈ spt T and ρ > 0. Fix an IMRep R = (M_R, θ_R, ξ_R) of T (T is integer multiplicity). By region_support_cycle, x ∈ spt T ⊆ U ∩ N.
1. (Graph chart of N at x.)
(1a) Tangent plane. IsOrientation (n+1) N ξ_N at x gives a subspace Π with Π = tangentSpace(N, x) (as sets) and IsUnitOrientationOf(ξ_N(x), Π). The orthonormal family in that definition has n + 1 vectors and spans Π, so dim Π = n + 1. Put ξ_Π := ξ_N(x), p := orthogonal projection onto Π and p^⊥ := I − p.
(1b) The chart is a homeomorphism. Take a chart (V, W, ψ) of N at x (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+1) N) and z₀ ∈ V with ψ(z₀) = x. ψ : V → W ∩ N is a continuous bijection, and V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. A continuous map from V into the locally compact Hausdorff space W with this property is a closed map into W. Hence ψ maps relatively closed subsets of V onto relatively closed subsets of W ∩ N (in particular W ∩ N = ψ(V) is closed in W), and the continuous bijection ψ : V → W ∩ N is a homeomorphism.
(1c) The derivative has range Π. For v ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and small ε > 0, t ↦ ψ(z₀ + εtv) (t ∈ (−1, 1)) is a C¹ curve in N through x with derivative εDψ(z₀)v at t = 0; so range Dψ(z₀) ⊆ tangentSpace(N, x) = Π. Dψ(z₀) is injective and dim Π = n + 1, so range Dψ(z₀) = Π.
(1d) The graph map u. p∘(ψ − x) has invertible derivative p∘Dψ(z₀) : ℝ^{n+1} → Π at z₀. By the inverse function theorem it is a C² diffeomorphism of an open V₀ ∋ z₀ onto an open neighbourhood O of 0 in Π. ψ(V₀) is relatively open in W ∩ N by (1b), so ψ(V₀) ⊇ N ∩ B_s(x) for some s > 0. Put u := p^⊥∘(ψ − x)∘(p∘(ψ − x)|_{V₀})^{−1} : O → Π^⊥; it is C², u(0) = 0, and Du(0) = 0 because range Dψ(z₀) = Π. Choose r₁ > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r₁) ⊆ U ∩ W ∩ B_s(x), put δ₂ := r₁, and choose δ₁ ∈ (0, r₁) such that D := Π ∩ B_{δ₁}(0) ⊆ O, |Du| ≤ 1 on D and |u| < δ₂/2 on D. The open cylinder Z := {x + v + h : v ∈ Π, |v| < δ₁, h ∈ Π^⊥, |h| < δ₂} has closure in closedBall(x, √2·r₁); so closure Z is compact and contained in U ∩ W ∩ B_s(x).
(1e) The parametrization G. Put G(v) := x + v + u(v) for v ∈ D. Then N ∩ Z = G(D): a point q ∈ N ∩ Z lies in N ∩ B_s(x) ⊆ ψ(V₀), so v := p(q − x) ∈ O with |v| < δ₁ and p^⊥(q − x) = u(v), i.e. q = G(v) with v ∈ D; conversely G(v) = ψ((p∘(ψ − x)|_{V₀})^{−1}(v)) ∈ N and |u(v)| < δ₂, so G(D) ⊆ N ∩ Z. G is an injective C² map with p(G(v) − x) = v and DG(v) = I + Du(v) on Π. In particular N ∩ Z is relatively closed in Z, being the graph of a continuous map over D intersected with Z. Applying (1c) to the parametrization G at v (for t ↦ G(v + εtw) and, conversely, writing a C¹ curve γ in N through G(v) as γ = G∘(p∘(γ − x)) near t = 0) gives tangentSpace(N, G(v)) = DG(v)Π.
(1f) Orientation. Put J(v) := det(DG(v)τ_i · DG(v)τ_j)^{1/2} > 0 for an orthonormal basis τ of Π with ξ_Π(β) = ±β(τ), and η(v) := Λ_{n+1}DG(v)ξ_Π/J(v), i.e. η(v)(α) := ξ_Π(α(DG(v)·, …, DG(v)·))/J(v). Then ξ_N(G(v)) = η(v) for every v ∈ D:
- η(v) is a unit orientation of DG(v)Π: Gram–Schmidt writes (DG(v)τ_1, …, DG(v)τ_{n+1}) = σU with σ an orthonormal basis of DG(v)Π and U upper triangular with positive diagonal; by multilinearity and alternation α(DG(v)τ) = det(U)·α(σ), and J(v) = det(UᵀU)^{1/2} = det U. So η(v)(α) = ±α(σ).
- ξ_N(G(v)) is a unit orientation of tangentSpace(N, G(v)) = DG(v)Π (IsOrientation). By orientation_sign, ξ_N(G(v)) = s(v)·η(v) with s(v) ∈ {1, −1}.
- With L from unit_orientation_dual, s(v) = ξ_N(G(v))(L(η(v))), because η(v)(L(η(v))) = 1. The right side is continuous in v ∈ D: ξ_N is continuous on N, G and DG are continuous (u ∈ C²), J > 0 is continuous, L is continuous linear, and evaluation is continuous. D is connected, so s is constant, and s(0) = 1 because G(0) = x, DG(0) = I on Π and η(0) = ξ_Π = ξ_N(x).
2. (Local formula.) Let F := {v ∈ D : G(v) ∈ E}; F is Borel (E is measurable and G continuous) and E ∩ Z = G(F), because E ⊆ N. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ Z.
- dω vanishes off tsupport ω ⊆ Z. The area formula for the injective C¹ map G (SimonGMT injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative), with Jacobian J, and (1f) give
 T(ω) = ∫_{E∩Z} ξ_N(dω) dH^{n+1} = ∫_F ξ_N(G(v))(dω(G(v)))J(v) dv = ∫_F ξ_Π((G^#dω)(v)) dv.
- G^{−1}(tsupport ω) = p((tsupport ω ∩ N) − x) is compact (tsupport ω ∩ N is closed in the compact tsupport ω, because N ∩ Z is relatively closed in Z), so G^#ω is a compactly supported C¹ n-form on D, and G^#dω = d(G^#ω) (G is C²).
- Identify Π with ℝ^{n+1} by a linear isometry carrying ξ_Π to e_1∧⋯∧e_{n+1}. A compactly supported C¹ n-form β on D is β = Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}φ_j dv^1∧⋯∧\widehat{dv^j}∧⋯∧dv^{n+1} for a vector field φ_β = (φ_1, …, φ_{n+1}), with |β| = |φ_β| and ξ_Π(dβ) = div φ_β.
- Hence (*) T(ω) = ∫_F div φ_{G^#ω} dv.
3. (Locally finite perimeter; Simon Ch. 6, 2.35.) For 0 < s' < δ₁ put D_{s'} := Π ∩ B_{s'}(0) and Z_{s'} := {w ∈ Z : |p(w − x)| < s'}.
- Fix χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on (−∞, δ₂/2] and χ = 0 on [3δ₂/4, ∞). Put ζ(w) := χ(|p^⊥(w − x)|), smooth because χ is constant near 0, and π(w) := p(w − x).
- Let φ be a smooth vector field with compact support in D_{s'} and |φ| ≤ 1, with corresponding n-form β, and put ω_φ := ζ·π^#β. Then ω_φ is smooth, tsupport ω_φ ⊆ {w : π(w) ∈ spt φ, |p^⊥(w − x)| ≤ 3δ₂/4} is a compact subset of Z_{s'}, so ω_φ ∈ 𝒟^n(U), and G^#ω_φ = β (π∘G = id and ζ∘G = 1 on D, as |u| < δ₂/2).
- |ω_φ| ≤ 1. Choose an orthonormal basis f_1, …, f_P of ℝ^P whose first n + 1 vectors are those of the isometry Π ≅ ℝ^{n+1}. In the basis of increasing wedges of the f's, the coefficients of ω_φ(w) = ζ(w)·β(π(w))∘p are ζ(w) times those of β(π(w)) for index sets inside {1, …, n+1} and 0 otherwise; so their square sum is ζ(w)²|φ(π(w))|² ≤ 1. The Euclidean coefficient norm does not depend on the orthonormal basis: coefficients transform by the n-th compound matrix C_n(O) of the orthogonal change-of-basis matrix O, and C_n(O)C_n(O)ᵀ = C_n(OOᵀ) = I by the Cauchy–Binet formula. (Only a bound |ω_φ| ≤ c₀ with c₀ independent of φ is needed below, and such a bound is immediate since the coefficients of ω_φ depend linearly on φ.)
- So ω_φ is admissible for M_{Z_{s'}}(T). By (*) and oriented_piece_mass (first conclusion) applied to the representation R (V := U, M' := M_R, θ' := θ_R, ξ' := ξ_R, W := Z_{s'}):
 ∫_F div φ = T(ω_φ) ≤ M_{Z_{s'}}(T) ≤ ∫_{M_R∩Z_{s'}} θ_R dH^n ≤ μ_R(closure Z) < ∞;
 the same holds for −φ.
- Smooth fields suffice in the definition of the variation (mollify a C¹ field; supports stay in D_{s'} and |φ| ≤ 1 is preserved). So |D1_F|(D_{s'}) ≤ μ_R(closure Z) < ∞ for every s' < δ₁, and F has locally finite perimeter in D.
4. (De Giorgi; Simon Ch. 3, 4.3.) The reduced boundary ∂*F is countably n-rectifiable, |D1_F| = H^n⌞∂*F on D, and with the measure-theoretic inner normal ν_F, ∫_F div φ = −∫_{∂*F} φ·ν_F dH^n for compactly supported C¹ fields φ on D. Since H^n is Borel regular and H^n(∂*F ∩ D_{s'}) < ∞, fix a Borel set B ⊆ D with ∂*F ∩ D ⊆ B and H^n(B ∖ ∂*F) = 0; all integrals over ∂*F below are integrals over B. For v ∈ ∂*F let ξ_F(v) be the unit simple n-vector of the plane ν_F(v)^⊥ ⊆ Π with ξ_F(v)(β) = −φ_β(v)·ν_F(v) for n-covectors β on Π. Then ∫_F ξ_Π(dβ) = ∫_{∂*F} ξ_F(β) dH^n.
5. (Multiplicity-one representation.) Put D' := D_{δ₁/2}, Z₀ := Z_{δ₁/2} (an open set containing x) and M' := G(B ∩ D') = {w ∈ N ∩ Z : p(w − x) ∈ B ∩ D'}, a Borel set (N ∩ Z is relatively closed in Z) with M' ⊆ Z₀.
- Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ Z₀; then G^#ω has support in D'. By (*), step 4 with β = G^#ω, and the area formula for G on the rectifiable set B ∩ D' (Simon Ch. 3, 2.4–2.7, with Jacobian J'(v) := |Λ_nDG(v)ξ_F(v)| > 0),
 T(ω) = ∫_{M'} ξ'(w)(ω(w)) dH^n(w), where ξ'(G(v)) := Λ_nDG(v)ξ_F(v)/J'(v).
- M' is countably n-rectifiable (a Lipschitz image of a rectifiable set), and ξ' is a measurable field of unit simple n-vectors, i.e. ξ'(w) is a unit orientation of an n-plane (Gram–Schmidt as in (1f)).
- H^n(M') = ∫_{B∩D'} J' dH^n ≤ 2^{n/2}·|D1_F|(D') < ∞, because |Du| ≤ 1 gives ‖DG‖ ≤ √2, hence J' ≤ ‖DG‖^n ≤ 2^{n/2}.
- By oriented_piece_mass (second conclusion) with V := Z₀, θ' :≡ 1 and this M', ξ': M_W(T) = H^n(M' ∩ W) for every open W ⊆ Z₀.
6. (Density one a.e. on M'.) By (G7), for H^n-a.e. w ∈ M', H^n(M' ∩ B_t(w))/(ω_nt^n) → 1 as t ↓ 0. For such w, B_t(w) ⊆ Z₀ for small t (w ∈ M' ⊆ Z₀, Z₀ open), so step 5 gives M_{B_t(w)}(T) = H^n(M' ∩ B_t(w)); hence Θ^n(μ_T, w) = 1.
7. (Conclusion.)
- W' := Z₀ ∩ B_ρ(x) is open, contains x, and has compact closure in U.
- By (G3), M_{W'}(T) > 0, so H^n(M' ∩ W') > 0 by step 5.
- The exceptional set of step 6 is H^n-null, so some w ∈ M' ∩ W' has Θ^n(μ_T, w) = 1.
- By (G2), w ∈ spt T. So y := w ∈ spt T ∩ B_ρ(x) and HasMassDensity T y 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: spt T ⊆ N (region_support_cycle); near x ∈ spt T, N is a C² graph G(v) = x + v + u(v) over T_xN with ξ_N(G(v)) = Λ_{n+1}DG(v)ξ_N(x)/J(v) (orientation_sign, and continuity of the sign via unit_orientation_dual).
In the chart, T(ω) = ∫_F div φ_{G^#ω} with F = G^{−1}(E); testing with ζ·π^#β and the mass bound of oriented_piece_mass for an IMRep of T gives finite perimeter of F (Simon 6.2.35).
De Giorgi's structure theorem writes T = [[G(∂*F)]] with multiplicity one near x; oriented_piece_mass gives M_W(T) = H^n(G(∂*F) ∩ W).
Rectifiable sets have density one a.e., and positive mass near x forces a density-one point of spt T in every ball about x.

subproblem.title: Simons' theorem for minimizing hypercones that are regular with multiplicity one off the vertex (Simon B.1–B.2)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (A₀ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 2 ≤ m → m ≤ 6 → Module.finrank ℝ A₀ = m + 1 → IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → IsConeCurrent C → C.support ⊆ (A₀ : Set (Euclid P)) → (∀ y ∈ C.support, y ≠ 0 → y ∈ regularSet C ∧ HasMassDensity C y 1) → ∀ θ : ℝ, HasMassDensity C 0 θ → θ ≤ 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 5 (β)–(γ) of the supplied proof of CodimensionOneRegularity for the cone factor S₀: Simon Appendix B, B.1, B.2 and the printed proof of B.2 (Simons [Sim68], in the form of Schoen–Simon–Yau; chapter-07-source.txt lines 1256–1539 = chapter-B.txt lines 1–233), together with the verification of the hypotheses of B.2. General facts (for a current T ∈ 𝒟_m(U), U open).
(G1) Uniqueness of densities. If Θ^m(μ_T, y) = θ₁ and Θ^m(μ_T, y) = θ₂, then θ₁ = θ₂, because limits in [0, ∞] are unique and ofReal is injective on [0, ∞).
(G2) Positive density forces support. If T vanishes on an open W, then M_{W'}(T) = 0 for every W' ⊆ W. Hence if y ∈ U has Θ^m(μ_T, y) = θ > 0, then y ∈ spt T: otherwise y lies in an open W on which T vanishes, M_{B_t(y)}(T) = 0 for small t, and the density is 0 ≠ θ.
(G7) Density of C¹ submanifolds (Simon Ch. 3, 1.8–1.9). If M' ∩ B_r(w) is a relatively closed embedded C¹ m-submanifold of B_r(w) containing w, then H^m(M' ∩ B_s(w))/(ω_ms^m) → 1 as s ↓ 0: near w, M' is the graph over T_wM' of a C¹ map whose Lipschitz constant on B_s(w) tends to 0 as s ↓ 0, and the area formula gives H^m(M' ∩ B_s(w)) = ω_ms^m(1 + o(1)).

Proof. Fix P, m, C, A₀ satisfying the hypotheses, and let θ satisfy Θ^m(μ_C, 0) = θ.

B0. (Set-up.)
- dim A₀ = m + 1 ≤ P.
- C is integer multiplicity (first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn). Fix an IMRep R = (M_R, θ_R, ξ_R) of C and put μ := μ_R; then μ(K) < ∞ for compact K (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult).
- The general facts (G1), (G2), (G7) above hold with U := ℝ^P.
(B0.1) Vertex negligibility. Let χ_ε ∈ C^∞_c(B_{2ε}(0)) with 0 ≤ χ_ε ≤ 1 and χ_ε = 1 on B_ε(0). For every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), C(χ_εω) → 0 as ε ↓ 0.
- C(χ_εω) = ∫_{M_R} θ_Rχ_ε⟨ω, ξ_R⟩ dH^m.
- For ε ≤ 1/2 the integrand is dominated by θ_R·max|ω|·1_{B_1(0)}, because ξ_R(x) is a unit orientation of a plane for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M_R (IMRep.orients) and then |ξ_R(x)(α)| ≤ |α| by unit_orientation_dual (a); the dominant is integrable since μ(closedBall(0, 1)) < ∞.
- It tends pointwise to θ_R1_{{0}}⟨ω, ξ_R⟩, and H^m({0}) = 0 because m ≥ 1. Dominated convergence gives the limit 0.
- Since (1 − χ_ε)ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport ⊆ tsupport ω ∖ B_ε(0), it follows that C(ω) = lim_{ε↓0} C((1 − χ_ε)ω).

B1. (Trivial case M = ∅.) Then spt C ⊆ {0}.
- For every ω, tsupport((1 − χ_ε)ω) is disjoint from {0} ⊇ spt C, so C((1 − χ_ε)ω) = 0 by vanish_off_support.
- By (B0.1), C(ω) = 0 for every ω. Thus C = 0, M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = 0 for every ρ, and Θ^m(μ_C, 0) = 0.
- By (G1), θ = 0 ≤ 1. From now on assume M ≠ ∅.

B2. (Local structure of M; parent 5(β)(i).) Let y ∈ M. By hypothesis y ∈ regularSet C and Θ^m(μ_C, y) = 1. The definition of regularSet gives:
- ρ_y > 0, m_y ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, and an embedded C¹ m-dimensional submanifold M_y ∋ y;
- an orientation ξ_y of M_y: continuous on M_y, with ξ_y(w) a unit orientation of tangentSpace(M_y, w);
- H^m(M_y ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ B_{ρ_y}(y);
- C(ω) = m_y ∫_{M_y} ⟨ω, ξ_y⟩ dH^m whenever tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ_y}(y).
(B2a) Relative closedness.
- Take a chart (V, W_ψ, ψ) of M_y at y. Since ψ(V) = W_ψ ∩ M_y and ψ is proper, W_ψ ∩ M_y is closed in W_ψ.
- Choose ρ' with 0 < ρ' ≤ min(ρ_y, |y|)/2 and B_{2ρ'}(y) ⊆ W_ψ.
- Then M_y ∩ B_{ρ'}(y) is relatively closed in B_{ρ'}(y), and 0 ∉ closedBall(y, ρ').
(B2b) If tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ'}(y) ∖ M_y, an open set, then ω = 0 on M_y and C(ω) = 0. So spt C ∩ B_{ρ'}(y) ⊆ M_y.
(B2c) Mass identity. Apply oriented_piece_mass (second conclusion) with θ' :≡ |m_y|, V := B_{ρ'}(y), M' := M_y ∩ B_{ρ'}(y) and ξ' := sign(m_y)ξ_y (extended by 0 off M'). Its hypotheses hold:
- M' is Borel, being relatively closed in the open ball;
- ξ' is continuous on the Borel set M', hence measurable, and sign(m_y)ξ_y(w) is a unit orientation of tangentSpace(M_y, w) for every w ∈ M';
- C(ω) = m_y∫_{M_y}⟨ω, ξ_y⟩ dH^m = |m_y|∫_{M'}⟨ω, sign(m_y)ξ_y⟩ dH^m whenever tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ'}(y);
- for open W ⊆ B_{ρ'}(y), ∫_{M'∩W} |m_y| dH^m = |m_y|·H^m(M_y ∩ W) ≤ |m_y|·H^m(M_y ∩ closedBall(y, ρ')) < ∞, since closedBall(y, ρ') is a compact subset of B_{ρ_y}(y).
This gives M_W(C) = |m_y|·H^m(M_y ∩ W) for every open W ⊆ B_{ρ'}(y).
(B2d) Densities.
- By (B2c) and (G7) (C¹ case), Θ^m(μ_C, w) = |m_y| for every w ∈ M_y ∩ B_{ρ'}(y).
- In particular |m_y| = Θ^m(μ_C, y) = 1 by (G1).
- Every such w has density 1 > 0, so w ∈ spt C by (G2).
(B2e) Consequences.
- M ∩ B_{ρ'}(y) = M_y ∩ B_{ρ'}(y), and this set lies in A₀ since spt C ⊆ A₀.
- C(ω) = ∫_M ⟨ω, ξ'_y⟩ dH^m for tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ'}(y), where ξ'_y := m_yξ_y is a continuous unit orientation.
- M_W(C) = H^m(M ∩ W) for open W ⊆ B_{ρ'}(y).
- Hence M is an embedded C¹ m-submanifold of ℝ^P contained in the (m+1)-dimensional subspace A₀, i.e. a C¹ hypersurface of A₀ ∖ {0}. It is relatively closed in ℝ^P ∖ {0}, because spt C is closed.

B3. (Global orientation and representation off the vertex.)
(B3a) Agreement on overlaps. If B_{ρ'}(y) ∩ B_{ρ'}(y') ≠ ∅, then ∫_M ⟨ω, ξ'_y − ξ'_{y'}⟩ dH^m = 0 for every ω supported in the overlap. Test with ω = φβ, where φ ranges over C^∞_c and β over a countable dense set of constant covectors. This gives ξ'_y = ξ'_{y'} H^m-a.e. on M in the overlap.
(B3b) A continuous global orientation. The set where ξ'_y ≠ ξ'_{y'} is relatively open in M and H^m-null. A nonempty relatively open subset of a C¹ m-submanifold has positive H^m-measure, so the two orientations agree everywhere on the overlap. This defines a continuous unit orientation ξ_M of M.
(B3c) Representation off the vertex. Let ω have tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ {0}.
- Cover the compact set tsupport ω by finitely many balls B_{ρ'}(y_j), y_j ∈ M, together with the open set ℝ^P ∖ spt C.
- Take a smooth partition of unity subordinate to this cover. On pieces supported in ℝ^P ∖ spt C both sides vanish, by vanish_off_support and because M ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ spt C) = ∅.
- Hence (†) C(ω) = ∫_M ⟨ω, ξ_M⟩ dH^m for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ {0}.
(B3d) Finiteness and mass off the vertex.
- For W open with compact closure in ℝ^P ∖ {0}, H^m(M ∩ W) < ∞, since finitely many balls B_{ρ'}(y_j) cover M ∩ closure(W).
- M is relatively closed in the open set ℝ^P ∖ {0}, hence Borel, and ξ_M (extended by 0 off M) is measurable. By oriented_piece_mass (second conclusion) with θ' :≡ 1, V := ℝ^P ∖ {0}, M' := M and ξ' := ξ_M, using (†): M_W(C) = H^m(M ∩ W) for such W.
- For 0 < ε < ρ, W_ε := B_ρ(0) ∖ closedBall(0, ε) is such a W, and oriented_piece_mass (first conclusion) applied to the representation R gives M_{W_ε}(C) ≤ ∫_{M_R∩W_ε} θ_R dH^m ≤ μ(closedBall(0, ρ)) < ∞. So H^m(M ∩ W_ε) ≤ μ(closedBall(0, ρ)); letting ε ↓ 0 (monotone convergence, 0 ∉ M) gives H^m(M ∩ B_ρ(0)) < ∞ for every ρ.

B4. (Cone structure; parent 5(β)(iii)–(iv).)
- Let t > 0 and let W be an open set with compact closure on which C vanishes. Then C vanishes on tW. Indeed, let tsupport ω ⊆ tW. The sibling child cone_pullback_identity with λ := t^{−1} gives ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with ω'(z) = t^{m}ω(tz) and C(ω') = C(ω). Since tsupport ω' = t^{−1}tsupport ω ⊆ W, we get C(ω) = C(ω') = 0.
- closure(tW) = t·closure(W) is compact. Hence Z(C) is invariant under all dilations, and so is spt C = ℝ^P ∖ Z(C). Thus M = tM for all t > 0: M is a cone.
- 0 ∈ closure(M), because ty → 0 as t ↓ 0 for y ∈ M. Also closure(M) ⊆ spt C = M ∪ {0} and 0 ∉ M. Hence closure(M) ∖ M = {0}.

B5. (Competitors and first variation; stationarity.)
(B5a) Deformation. Let Z ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P ∖ {0}; ℝ^P), put K_Z := spt Z, and choose an open W with compact closure in ℝ^P ∖ {0} and K_Z ⊆ W.
- For |t| < t₀ := 1/(1 + 2 sup|DZ|), the map Φ_t := id + tZ is a C^∞ diffeomorphism of ℝ^P equal to the identity off K_Z.
- Hence Φ_t(K_Z) = K_Z and Φ_t(W) = W. If Z(w) ∈ A₀ for all w, then also Φ_t(A₀) = A₀.
(B5b) The push-forward is a current. S_t(ω) := C(Φ_t^#ω), the push-forward Φ_{t#}C (Simon 6.2.23).
- Φ_t is proper, so Φ_t^# maps 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) into itself.
- Φ_t^# is sequentially continuous in the test-form topology: supports stay in Φ_t^{−1}(K), and derivatives converge uniformly by the chain rule. So S_t ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P).
(B5c) S_t is an admissible competitor.
- Integer multiplicity. By the area formula on the rectifiable set M_R (Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9), S_t is represented by (Φ_t(M_R), θ_R∘Φ_t^{−1}, ξ_t) with ξ_t(Φ_t x) := Λ_mDΦ_t(x)ξ_R(x)/|Λ_mDΦ_t(x)ξ_R(x)|. Here Φ_t(M_R) is Borel and countably m-rectifiable, its approximate tangent space at Φ_t(x) is DΦ_t(x)(T_xM_R), and the multiplicity is locally integrable since the Jacobians are bounded.
- Same boundary. m ≥ 2, so S_t(dφ) = C(Φ_t^#dφ) = C(d(Φ_t^#φ)) = 0 = C(dφ), using ∂C = 0.
- Compact support of the difference. If tsupport ω ∩ K_Z = ∅, then Φ_t^#ω = ω: at points off K_Z the map Φ_t is the identity nearby, and at points of K_Z both sides vanish because Φ_t(K_Z) = K_Z. So spt(S_t − C) ⊆ K_Z, a compact subset of W.
- Minimality of C in ℝ^P therefore gives M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S_t).
(B5d) Both masses are areas.
- For tsupport ω ⊆ W: S_t(ω) = C(Φ_t^#ω), with tsupport Φ_t^#ω ⊆ W ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ {0}.
- By (†) and the area formula for the injective smooth map Φ_t, S_t(ω) = ∫_{Φ_t(M)} ⟨ω, ξ_{M,t}⟩ dH^m, with ξ_{M,t} the transported unit orientation.
- Φ_t(M) ∩ W = Φ_t(M ∩ W) is Borel with finite H^m-measure (Φ_t is a diffeomorphism with Φ_t(W) = W, and H^m(M ∩ W) < ∞ by (B3d)), and ξ_{M,t} is measurable. By oriented_piece_mass (second conclusion) with θ' :≡ 1, V := W, M' := Φ_t(M) ∩ W and ξ' := ξ_{M,t}, M_W(S_t) = H^m(Φ_t(M) ∩ W) = H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ W)); by (B3d), M_W(C) = H^m(M ∩ W).
- So f_Z(t) := H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ W)) satisfies f_Z(t) ≥ f_Z(0) for |t| < t₀.
(B5e) First variation.
- By the area formula, f_Z(t) = ∫_{M∩W} J_t dH^m with J_t(x) := |(τ_1 + tDZ(x)τ_1)∧⋯∧(τ_m + tDZ(x)τ_m)|, for τ an orthonormal basis of T_xM.
- J_t(x) is smooth in t with derivatives bounded uniformly in x ∈ K_Z, J_t = 1 off K_Z, and ∂_tJ_t|_{t=0} = Σ_i τ_i·DZ(x)τ_i = div_M Z(x) (Simon Ch. 2, 5.1–5.3).
- So f_Z is differentiable at 0 with f_Z'(0) = ∫_M div_M Z dH^m. Since 0 is an interior minimum, ∫_M div_M Z dH^m = 0.
- For X ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^P ∖ {0}; ℝ^P), mollification gives such Z → X in C¹ with supports in a fixed compact set. Since H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ (B3d), ∫_M div_M X dH^m = 0.
- Hence the varifold V := v(M, 1) is stationary in ℝ^P ∖ {0} (Simon Ch. 2, 5.7–5.8).

B6. (Smoothness and zero mean curvature; parent 5(β)(ii).)
- Apply Simon Ch. 5, Theorem 7.1, last part, in the open set ℝ^P ∖ {0} with N := ℝ^P (C^∞). Its hypotheses hold: V is stationary, θ ≡ 1, and Θ^m(V, y) = 1 at every y ∈ M by (G7).
- So for each y ∈ M and each q there is σ_q > 0 such that, after a rigid motion, spt V ∩ B_{σ_q}(y) = M ∩ B_{σ_q}(y) is the graph of a C^{q+2,α} function. This holds at every y ∈ M and for every q, so M is a C^∞ submanifold.
- Since V is stationary and M is smooth, the first variation formula (Simon Ch. 2, 4.29 and 5.10) gives ∫_M X·H_M dH^m = 0 for all X ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^P ∖ {0}; ℝ^P). So the mean curvature H_M ≡ 0.
- As M ⊆ A₀, M is a smooth minimal hypersurface of A₀ ∖ {0}, with closure(M) ∖ M = {0} (B4).

B7. (Stability B.1; parent 5(β)(v); Simon Ch. 2, 5.11–5.12.)
(B7a) Unit normal. Fix an orientation of A₀ and let ν be the unit normal of M in A₀ determined by ξ_M; ν is smooth on M.
(B7b) The variation field. Let ζ ∈ C^∞_c(M), with support K ⊆ M compact. Let Z ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P ∖ {0}; ℝ^P) satisfy Z(w) ∈ A₀ for all w and Z = ζν on M. It exists:
- extend ζν to a smooth A₀-valued map near K, by local extensions and a partition of unity;
- compose with the orthogonal projection onto A₀;
- multiply by a cutoff equal to 1 near K with compact support in ℝ^P ∖ {0}.
(B7c) Minimality at t = 0. With W and Φ_t as in (B5a), Φ_t(A₀) = A₀. By (B5d), f(t) := H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ W)) has a minimum at t = 0. f is C^∞ near 0:
- J_t² is a polynomial in t whose coefficients are bounded on M ∩ K_Z, and J_t² ≥ 1/2 for |t| small.
- So J_t is C^∞ in t with t-derivatives bounded uniformly on M ∩ K_Z, and J_t = 1 off K_Z.
- Since H^m(M ∩ W) < ∞, f may be differentiated under the integral.
Hence f'(0) = 0 and f''(0) ≥ 0.
(B7d) Second variation. Apply the second variation formula (Simon Ch. 2, 5.4 and 5.11) to the smooth stationary M:
- The acceleration ∂²Φ_t/∂t² vanishes. The variation field Z|_M = ζν is normal to M.
- (D_{τ_i}(ζν))^⊥ = (∇_{τ_i}ζ)ν. Indeed D_{τ_i}ν ∈ A₀ is orthogonal to ν, hence tangent to M.
- B(τ_i, τ_j) = h_{ij}ν, where A = (h_{ij}) is the second fundamental form of M in A₀.
- So f''(0) = ∫_M (|∇^Mζ|² − |A|²ζ²) dH^m (Simon 5.12 (‡)).
(B7e) Conclusion. B.1 holds: ∫_M (|∇^Mζ|² − |A|²ζ²) dH^m ≥ 0 for every ζ ∈ C^∞_c(M). By mollification in charts it extends to locally Lipschitz ζ with compact support in M: |A| is continuous on M, and the supports stay in a fixed compact subset of M.

B8. (Simons' theorem B.2: the printed proof.) Identify A₀ with ℝ^{m+1} by a linear isometry. Then M is a smooth m-dimensional cone in ℝ^{m+1} with zero mean curvature, closure(M) ∖ M = {0}, stable in the sense of B.1, and 2 ≤ m ≤ 6. We show |A| ≡ 0 on M.

- For a cone, Lemma B.11 gives Σ_{i,j,k} h²_{ij;k} − |∇_M|A||² ≥ 2r^{−2}|A|² wherever |A| > 0. Choose τ_m radial along the ray through x; then h_{mj} = 0 and h_{ij;m} = −r^{−1}h_{ij} by homogeneity. The algebra is SimonGMT AppendixB.simonsDefect_eq_sum_skew, four_mul_radialSkewSum_le and cone_simonsDefect_lower_bound.

(B8d) Cone integrals.
- Σ := M ∩ ∂B_1(0) is a compact smooth (m−1)-dimensional submanifold. It is closed because closure(M) ∩ ∂B_1(0) = M ∩ ∂B_1(0), and the sphere is transversal to the cone M.
- (5) ∫_M f dH^m = ∫_0^∞ r^{m−1}∫_Σ f(rσ) dH^{m−1}(σ) dr for continuous f ≥ 0 on M.

- Choose ε > 0 with (m/2 − 2 + ε)² < 2 and (1 + ε)² < 2. This is possible exactly because 2 ≤ m ≤ 6, e.g. ε = 1/10 (SimonGMT AppendixB.exists_final_exponent).

B9. (Hyperplane.)
- |A| ≡ 0 means ν is locally constant on M. So each connected component M_c of M lies in an affine hyperplane of A₀.
- That hyperplane passes through 0. The ray through a point of M_c is connected, lies in M (B4) and meets M_c, so it lies in M_c. Hence M_c ⊆ H_c for an m-dimensional linear subspace H_c ⊆ A₀.
- M_c is open in H_c, being an m-submanifold of the m-plane H_c. It is closed in H_c ∖ {0}, since M is relatively closed in ℝ^P ∖ {0} and M_c is closed in M. H_c ∖ {0} is connected (m ≥ 2), so M_c = H_c ∖ {0}.
- Suppose two components had H_c ≠ H_{c'}. Then H_c ∩ H_{c'} has dimension m − 1 ≥ 1 and contains some w ≠ 0 lying in both M_c and M_{c'}, which is impossible.
- Hence M = H₀ ∖ {0} for a single m-dimensional linear subspace H₀ ⊆ A₀.

B10. (Density at the vertex.)
(B10a) Constant orientation. H₀ ∖ {0} is connected (m ≥ 2). For y ∈ M, ξ_M(y) is a unit orientation of tangentSpace(M, y) = H₀; fixing one unit orientation ξ_{H₀} of H₀, orientation_sign gives ξ_M(y) ∈ {ξ_{H₀}, −ξ_{H₀}}. (B10b) Global representation. For every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), (B0.1) and (†) give
